verdict.rationale: Statsig documents official Client and Server SDKs, including a JavaScript/React web SDK, and states that evaluation is deterministic, returning the same result across client and server platforms. That covers backend and web with consistent flag behavior. Mobile coverage is not shown: the evidence only mentions targeting mobile platforms in a gate, not an official mobile SDK. missing for 10: explicit documentation of official mobile (iOS/Android/React Native) SDKs, an enumerated list of supported backend languages, independent hands-on corroboration of cross-platform consistency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: Given the same user object and the same state of the experiment or feature gate, Statsig always returns the same result, even across different platforms (client or server).
Many customers deploy both Server and Client SDKs, which lets them gate features on both the client and server side.
Update your app's default function (typically App.tsx or Layout.tsx) so that the StatsigProvider component identifier wraps all child components.
After initialization, both Client and Server SDKs evaluate experiments/gates _without a network request_, and typically in less than 1ms.
